experiments.scope: Selected sha256-r37 target, organizer trial seeds. Each trial runs the proof's single-walk distinguished-point algorithm on g(x) = top 12 bits of the complete 37-round digest of a 48-byte message: a seed-dependent 32-byte template carrying x followed by a seed-dependent 16-byte suffix, walk cut off at k = 65 = (65/64)*2^6 steps, DP = top 1 of 12 bits zero, run bound 32, table capacity 256.
experiments.hypothesis: If the random-mapping premise RM-WALK holds for this truncation, the success frequency over 256 trials matches the ideal random-function rate for identical parameters (0.375 by simulation, proof Section 8). Pre-set decision rule: fewer than 78 of 256 successes (exact one-sided 1% binomial cut-off, not corrected for three widths) counts against the premise or the implementation.
